text:
Alex: quick follow-up from the RFC — proposing a lightweight 'hint layer' between router and policy engine. idea is to answer 70-80% of routing decisions with cheap heuristics and only invoke full policy for the rest. saves eval cost and lowers p99 when load spikes.
Maria: can you sketch what the hint layer exposes? is this another policy language or an API?
Alex: not a new lang. think of it as a compact interface: a set of graded hints (region_preference, cost_delta_estimate, latency_bucket) produced by fast heuristics or cached probes. router consults hints first, falls back to policy engine if hints are inconclusive.
Devon: examples?
Alex: e.g. hint = { region: "us-west", score: 0.85, confidence: 0.7 } where confidence < 0.5 => force full policy. confidence threshold tunable per route.
Jen: ok but how do we avoid divergence? hints could be stale and route things incorrectly under tight SLAs.
Alex: agreed — plan is to attach TTL + last_probe_ts and a provenance tag. strong guardrails: if hint.confidence < 0.6 or route is SLA-sensitive, skip hint. also catastrophic checks in runtime to reject hinted decisions if downstream telemetry shows error spike.
Maria: what about telemetry? we'll need to measure hit-rate, false positive rate (hints that would have changed decision) and cost savings.
TelemetryBot: automated metric scaffold created: hint_hit_rate, hint_reject_rate, hint_latency_savings, hint_mismatch_rate. hooking to per-route dashboards.
Devon: rollout strategy? big bang would be scary.
Alex: staged: 1) read-only mode (record decisions but always call policy) 2) advisory mode — router can prefer hint but still call policy in background and compare 3) canary rollout for low-SLA routes 4) gradual scale with per-tenant toggles.
Jen: sounds reasonable. curious about memory/cache pressure from storing hints per-key (prefix). any rough numbers?
Alex: benchmarks show a small prefetch cache per-route (LRU) at 100k entries reduces policy calls by ~40% for typical chat loads. entries are tiny (couple dozen bytes).
Maria: we need a migration plan for existing policy plugins. will plugin authors be forced to implement hint semantics?
Alex: no. default: runtime will synthesize hints from existing policy outputs during read-only period. plugin authors are encouraged to provide a fast_hint() hook for higher accuracy. fallback remains full policy.
Devon: how about testing harness? we need simulation to validate mismatch and oscillation effects.
Alex: wrote a small sim harness to replay traffic and inject capacity/latency perturbations. quick example to run locally:

```
# run replay sim for route "chat-gen"
./sim_runner --replay ./replays/chat_2026-02-14.log --hint-layer --compare-policy --output ./sim_out
```

Alex: sim emits per-request "hint_vs_policy" outcomes so we can compute mismatch_rate under different loads.
Jen: any concern about extra latency when hint path decides to call full policy? two-step could add serialization overhead.
Alex: microbenchmarks show hint eval adds ~200us when cached and <1ms cold. We batch background policy comparisons to amortize cost. net p50/p95 improves.
Maria: operational controls we need: per-route thresholds, global off switch, per-tenant opt-out, alerting on hint_mismatch_rate > X.
Alex: agreed — propose defaults: confidence_threshold=0.6, read_only=true initially, mismatch_alert=1% (configurable).
Devon: ownership and rollout checklist?
Alex: I'll own initial proto. next: docs for plugin authors, sim runs, telemetry dashboard, canary plan (dev/test workloads then small percentage of prod), post-mortem after 2 weeks.
Maria: include migration notes for Dedicated/Private where probes might be restricted.
Alex: yes — for Private, hints can be generated by a local probe service; if probes disabled, we fall back to cache-only hints synthesized from historical routing.
Jen: +1. let's schedule a follow-up demo after we have sim data.
Alex: thanks — I'll post sim results and updated rollout checklist next week. :thumbsup:
